title: Why tide pools stay alive
text: Tide pools are basins of seawater stranded on rocky shores when the ocean retreats. Over a few hours the trapped water warms, evaporates, and grows saltier, yet anemones, limpets, and tiny crabs survive. Their secret is adaptation: many clamp shut to retain moisture, and others tolerate sharp swings in temperature and salinity that would kill most marine animals.

title: The Lantern Bridge restoration
text: The Lantern Bridge, a 19th-century footbridge in the fictional town of Marrowby, was closed for two years while engineers replaced corroded iron ribs with galvanized steel. The council insisted the original cast lanterns be reinstalled, even though modern LED fixtures would have cost less and used far less electricity.

title: How sourdough rises
text: A sourdough starter is a living culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria suspended in flour and water. The yeast ferments sugars from the flour, releasing carbon dioxide that inflates the dough, while the bacteria produce acids that give the loaf its tang and help it keep longer than bread made with commercial yeast.
